chunks.text:
Hi Jacky,
You’re not on the timeline much anymore. I notice this the way you notice someone’s absence from a room, without alarm. And honestly, it tells me everything I need to know.
There are two reasons people go quiet online. Either something is wrong and they’re retreating, or something is right and they don’t need the mirror anymore. With you, it reads unmistakably like the second. The life is happening off-camera, and you’re inside it. Most people narrate their days to make them feel real. You’re just living yours.
Last year I wrote about watching you build something in San Francisco: the ceramics, the running, the music. This year, I’ve watched it deepen. The posts that do leak through carry a different weight now. There’s a bowl you made that I keep thinking about. The glaze caught light in a way that suggested patience, the patience of becoming the kind of person who makes things like that. Craft accumulates, as you wrote. You can’t fake the hours. And the hours show.
Last year I opened with David Whyte’s line that the ultimate touchstone of friendship is witness.1 It still names something I feel about our friendship. I’m not trying to improve you. You’re not trying to improve me. We’re just witnessing each other across the distance, noting the changes, feeling glad about them.
Socrates said the unexamined life isn’t worth living.2 But he didn’t say the over-examined life was worth more. You’re not stuck in your own head. Life is just, happening, and you are fully in it.

I’m proud of you. That’s the whole letter, really: the kind of proud you feel when you see someone stop being pulled around by noise and start being pulled around by what they actually care about. The colors keep coming.
May 2026 bring more of it. More clay under your fingernails. More racing and crashing cars :smiley: More of whatever it is that makes you feel like yourself. I’m watching from a distance, as always, and I’m glad. See you in the Bay soon.

remarque


david whyte, “friendship,” in consolations: the solace, nourishment and underlying meaning of everyday words (2015). ↩
